assignment.title: Your 90-Day AI Leadership Action Plan
assignment.format: One-page executive plan (worksheet template provided in the AI Strategy for Leaders Toolkit)
assignment.description: Develop a one-page executive plan covering the opportunity, the workflow to redesign, human + AI roles, governance and risk, success measures, and a 90-day Discover & Design / Pilot & Learn / Measure & Decide roadmap.

learningObjectives: Explain the evolution from traditional AI through generative AI to agentic AI
Distinguish AI assistants, copilots, agents, agentic workflows, and multi-agent systems
Explain AI opportunities and limitations in business language, not just technical language
Identify high-value AI opportunities within business processes and workflows
Evaluate AI initiatives using business value, feasibility, risk, and strategic importance
Determine appropriate roles for humans and AI within redesigned workflows
Understand how increasing AI autonomy requires increasing governance
Recognize the organizational, workforce, data, technology, and governance capabilities enterprise AI requires
Avoid the common mistakes that trap AI initiatives in endless experimentation
Develop a practical 90-Day AI Leadership Action Plan for your organization, team, or role
audience: Executives, business leaders, managers, consultants, technology leaders, transformation professionals, entrepreneurs, and aspiring AI leaders
title: AI Strategy for Leaders
description: From Generative AI to the Agentic Enterprise — a practical foundation for AI leadership. Learn where AI creates value, how to redesign work for humans and AI together, how to govern autonomy responsibly, and how to move from experimentation to execution.

curriculum.module: Module 1: The AI Shift — From Automation to Intelligence

topics.title: Lesson 1.1 — Why This AI Moment Is Different
topics.description: AI didn't begin with ChatGPT. This lesson traces the shift from traditional AI and predictive systems to generative, multimodal, reasoning-capable foundation models — and why declining barriers to adoption mean AI is becoming a general-purpose capability across knowledge work.

topics.title: Lesson 1.2 — The AI Capability Ladder™
topics.description: Introduces MyLearningLaunchpad's signature framework — Predict → Generate → Assist → Act → Collaborate → Orchestrate — showing how the leadership challenge shifts from technology adoption to delegation, governance, and organizational design as AI climbs the ladder.

A clear-eyed look at AI's real strengths (pattern recognition, generation, synthesis, reasoning, tool use) and real limits (hallucination, reliability, context, judgment, accountability) — the foundation for sound strategic decisions.
topics.title: Lesson 1.3 — What AI Can—and Cannot—Do
Module 1 Activity — AI Leadership Self-Assessment
topics.description: Score yourself and your organization across AI understanding, adoption, sponsorship, data readiness, workforce readiness, governance, workflow redesign, and measurement. This baseline carries through the rest of the course.

curriculum.module: Module 2: From Generative AI to Agentic AI

topics.description: Generative AI runs Prompt → Generate → Respond. Agentic AI runs Goal → Plan → Act → Observe → Evaluate → Adapt. This lesson unpacks the goals, planning, tools, memory, and autonomy that separate the two — and why the difference matters for leaders.
topics.title: Lesson 2.1 — Generative AI vs. Agentic AI
Lesson 2.2 — Copilots, Assistants and Agents
topics.description: A practical taxonomy — Assistant, Copilot, Agent, Agentic Workflow, Multi-Agent System — built around one leadership question: what authority are we actually giving the system?

Introduces the AI Autonomy Spectrum™ — from Human Does to AI Acts Autonomously — and the core principle that autonomy should be earned, not assumed, through evidence of reliability, controls, and trust.
topics.title: Lesson 2.3 — The Autonomy Spectrum
Lesson 2.4 — The Emerging Agentic Enterprise
topics.description: Explores how agentic systems could reshape customer service, finance, HR, IT, software development, supply chains, sales, and more — and why agentic AI shouldn't just be layered onto inefficient processes.
Choose one recurring workflow and decide what should remain human, what AI could assist with, what AI could execute, and what should never be delegated without approval.
topics.title: Module 2 Activity — The Delegation Exercise

curriculum.module: Module 3: Finding the Value — Where Should We Apply AI?

topics.title: Lesson 3.1 — Stop Starting With the Technology
topics.description: Reframes the wrong question ('Where can we use AI?') into the right one: where is valuable work constrained by time, cost, complexity, information, or human capacity? Start with business problems, not AI capabilities.
Four value domains — Productivity, Experience, Growth, and Transformation — give leaders a shared language for mapping where AI opportunities actually create value.
topics.title: Lesson 3.2 — The AI Value Map™
Lesson 3.3 — Think Workflow, Not Use Case
topics.description: Moves from isolated tasks ('summarize documents') to full workflow redesign, teaching leaders to identify triggers, inputs, decisions, actions, systems, bottlenecks, and exceptions across a process.
Introduces the AI Opportunity Matrix™ — scoring potential initiatives on business value, feasibility, risk, and strategic fit — to move beyond random experimentation toward systematic prioritization.
topics.title: Lesson 3.4 — Prioritizing AI Opportunities
Module 3 Activity — Find Your Top Three AI Opportunities
topics.description: Identify 5–10 opportunities, score them with the AI Opportunity Matrix, and select one priority workflow — this becomes the subject of your capstone.

curriculum.module: Module 4: Redesigning Work for Humans + AI

topics.title: Lesson 4.1 — Don't Automate a Bad Process
topics.description: Why organizations default to Digitize → Automate → Add AI without questioning the underlying process — and the better path: Understand → Eliminate → Simplify → Redesign → Augment → Automate.

AI excels at scale, speed, pattern recognition, and synthesis. Humans remain essential for accountability, ethical judgment, empathy, and strategic judgment. The goal isn't Human OR AI — it's Human × AI.
topics.title: Lesson 4.2 — Human + AI Comparative Advantage
Lesson 4.3 — The Human-Agent Operating Model™
topics.description: Four roles for redesigned work — AI Executes, AI Recommends, Human Decides, Human Governs — give leaders a shared vocabulary for allocating work between people and systems.
Take a real workflow from its 'before' state to an 'after' state built around human-in-the-loop and human-on-the-loop patterns, exception-based intervention, escalation, and approval gates.
topics.title: Lesson 4.4 — Redesigning the Workflow

topics.description: Redesign your selected workflow end-to-end: objective, trigger, human and AI roles, tools/data, decision points, approval gates, exceptions, escalation paths, and success metrics. One of the course's principal artifacts.
topics.title: Module 4 Activity — Human + AI Workflow Canvas™

curriculum.module: Module 5: Governing AI — Trust, Risk and Responsible Autonomy

topics.title: Lesson 5.1 — The New Risk Equation
topics.description: Capability ↑ + Autonomy ↑ = Governance ↑. As systems gain the ability to act, organizations must strengthen identity, permissions, monitoring, testing, auditability, and accountability.
Six dimensions of trustworthy AI — Reliability, Safety, Security, Privacy, Transparency, Accountability — give leaders a checklist for evaluating any AI system before it's given more authority.
topics.title: Lesson 5.2 — The AI Trust Stack™

topics.description: Returns to the Autonomy Spectrum with one governing principle: govern the decision and the consequence, not merely the model. A marketing-copy assistant and a transaction-approving agent don't need the same controls.
topics.title: Lesson 5.3 — Matching Governance to Autonomy
Lesson 5.4 — Responsible AI as a Leadership Responsibility
topics.description: Covers executive accountability, policy, risk ownership, AI governance bodies, model evaluation, data governance, workforce education, vendor considerations, and continuous monitoring.
For your priority workflow: what can the AI access or change, what decisions can it make, what requires approval, what happens on failure, and who monitors, stops, and owns the outcome?
topics.title: Module 5 Activity — AI Governance Checklist

curriculum.module: Module 6: From AI Ambition to Execution

topics.title: Lesson 6.1 — Why AI Pilots Don't Scale
topics.description: The common failure modes — technology-first thinking, no business owner, weak business case, poor data, missing integration, inadequate governance, no measurement — that trap initiatives in endless experimentation.

topics.title: Lesson 6.2 — The Enterprise AI Readiness Model™
topics.description: Six dimensions — Strategy, Work, Data, Technology, People, Governance — each scored from Emerging to AI-Native, giving leaders a structured view of organizational readiness.

A decision framework for commercial products, enterprise platforms, custom solutions, open-source models, and partners — build where AI creates distinctive advantage, buy where it's increasingly commodity.
topics.title: Lesson 6.3 — Build, Buy or Partner?

topics.description: Moves beyond 'did people use it?' to four measurement categories — Adoption, Performance, Operational Value, Strategic Value — that connect AI activity to business performance.
topics.title: Lesson 6.4 — Measuring AI Value

topics.description: The maturity progression from Experiment through Augment, Integrate, Delegate, Orchestrate, to Reimagine. AI maturity is measured by how deeply intelligence changes how the organization creates value — not by how many tools it owns.
topics.title: Lesson 6.5 — The Path to the AI-Native Enterprise

curriculum.module: Capstone: Your 90-Day AI Leadership Action Plan

topics.description: Define the business problem you're solving, why it matters, and what measurable outcome should improve.
topics.title: Part 1 — The Opportunity
Part 2 — The Workflow
topics.description: Identify the workflow you'll redesign and where the current bottlenecks are.
Decide what AI should assist, recommend, or execute — and what humans must decide, approve, or govern.
topics.title: Part 3 — Human + AI
Part 4 — Governance
topics.description: Identify the major risks, the authority AI can have, and the controls and human gates required.
Define 3–5 measurable indicators of success.
topics.title: Part 5 — Success Measures

topics.description: Days 1–30: Discover & Design. Days 31–60: Pilot & Learn. Days 61–90: Measure & Decide — stop, improve, expand, or scale.
topics.title: Part 6 — 90-Day Plan

fullDescription: AI leadership is no longer primarily about understanding what artificial intelligence can do. It is about deciding where AI should create value, which workflows should be redesigned, what decisions can be delegated, where humans must remain accountable, how AI should be governed, and how organizations move from experimentation to execution. This course provides leaders with a practical foundation for answering those questions. Rather than teaching a particular AI product, it develops the strategic frameworks required to lead organizations through the transition from generative AI toward increasingly agentic, AI-native ways of working. The competitive advantage from AI will not come simply from having access to better models — it will come from redesigning work, decisions, and organizations around what humans and intelligent systems can accomplish together. Every learner receives the AI Strategy for Leaders Toolkit — ten practical frameworks including the AI Capability Ladder, the Autonomy Spectrum, the AI Opportunity Matrix, and the Human + AI Workflow Canvas — plus a MyLearningLaunchpad Certificate of Completion.
